blocks.text: Remove your wine from yourself'. Then Hannah answered saying: 'It is not so, my lord; I am a woman with a heavy heart, I have drunk neither wine nor mead but I have poured out my soul before the Lord. Do not consider your handmaid as a worthless woman for it is owing to the abundance of my grief and distress that I have spoken so long'. Eli replied and said: 'Go forth in peace and the God of Israel will grant your request which you asked of Him'. She said: 'May your handmaid find favour in your eyes'. Then the woman went her way, she ate and her face was no longer sad. They rose early in the morning and prostrated themselves before the Lord, then they returned and arrived at their house in Ramah. And Elkanah knew his wife Hannah and the Lord remembered her; and in the course of time Hannah conceived and gave birth to a son. She called his name Samuel 'for I have asked for him of the Lord'. And the man Elkanah and the whole of his household went up to offer the annual sacrifice and his vow to the Lord. Hannah, however, did not go up, for she said to her husband: 'When the lad has been weaned, then I will bring him there that he may appear before the presence of the Lord and stay there for ever'. Her husband Elkanah said to her: 'Do what is best in your eyes, stay until you have weaned him; surely the Lord will fulfil His word'. The woman stayed and suckled her son until she had weaned him. Then she brought him up with her after she had weaned him, together with three bullocks, one ephah of flour and one bottle of wine. She brought him into the House of the Lord

notes: The Hebrew page has vowel points and some scattered accent-like marks, but not full cantillation. Following your instructions, I transcribed only consonants, vowels and dagesh. Where I could see an accent-like mark, I noted it as an uncertainty and did not add it to the text. I did not identify any of these marks as a rare accent with confidence. The possible telisha/pazer-shaped mark above וַתֹּאמֶר in 1:15 is the best candidate.
I did not transcribe metegs consistently; small vertical strokes below letters are hard to tell apart from tipcha/merkha-type marks at this resolution.
There are no qere/ketiv margin notes, Rashi instructions, aliyah labels, chapter labels, citation lines or English Hebrew-linkage words on either page.
Both pages start mid-verse in 1 Samuel 1:14 and end mid-verse in 1:24, continuing with 'שִׁלוֹ' / 'in Shiloh' on the next page.
